name: Finish Buggy Choke
description: Finishing a Buggy Choke uses the bottom player's same-side arm-and-leg loop around the top player's head and arm, closing space through body angle and shoulder-to-hip connection.
summary: Finishing a Buggy Choke uses the bottom player's same-side arm-and-leg loop around the top player's head and arm, closing space through body angle and shoulder-to-hip connection.
overview:
The bottom player is beneath side control with an arm connected to the same-side leg around the opponent's head and one arm. Top side control belongs to the choke defender. A half-guard finish requires its own leg configuration and is not automatically identical to the side-control setup.

Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg. Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Kade and Tye Ruotolo — OG Buggy Choke](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zixbOyLpoOc); [Jay Rodriguez — three Buggy Choke mistakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjKERx4N4mY).

attacker.name: Finish Buggy Choke Attacker
attacker.description: Finish Buggy Choke (attacker): Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg.
attacker.overview:
The bottom player is beneath side control with an arm connected to the same-side leg around the opponent's head and one arm. Top side control belongs to the choke defender. A half-guard finish requires its own leg configuration and is not automatically identical to the side-control setup.

Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg. Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.

Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee. Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost. Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

The arm-and-leg loop brings pressure to the sides of the neck as a vascular choke. Bring the shoulder toward the hip to shorten the enclosure; pulling the foot to create more force risks your own knee and does not substitute for closing the body angle.

Use the torso connection: Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee.
Recover guard when space opens: Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost.
Release if lifted: Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): How can you shorten the initial reach to your leg?
flashcards.answer: Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Use frames to turn partly onto your ribs

plausible: Stay flat and drag the foot toward the face
Extend your hips away while lifting the linking arm
trap: Keep the shoulder flat as you stretch the elbow upward

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): What belongs inside your same-side arm-leg loop?
flashcards.answer: Verify the head-and-one-arm configuration instead of assuming a grip on your own leg is enough.
flashcards.answer_line: The opponent's head and one arm

plausible: Only the opponent's head with both arms outside
Their near arm with the head beyond your elbow
trap: Only your own calf with their head free

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): What keeps the connecting reach compact?
flashcards.answer: Bring elbow and knee close through body position, not by forcing the foot inward.
flashcards.answer_line: Elbow close to the same-side knee

plausible: Elbow extended away from the knee
Both knees pinched while the linking elbow stays wide
trap: Hand close to the shin while the elbow stays flared

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): Which movement tightens the enclosure through the torso?
flashcards.answer: The closing action draws the shoulder toward the hip while the arm-leg connection contains head and arm.
flashcards.answer_line: Shorten the distance from shoulder to hip

plausible: Extend the ribs away from the hip
Lift the shoulder while keeping the hip stationary
trap: Slide the hips away while keeping your ribs extended

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): After they disengage and the loop fails, what do you recover first?
flashcards.answer: Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost.
flashcards.answer_line: Inside frames and knees for facing guard

plausible: Keep the same arm-leg grip while the shoulder line is flattened
Reach after the departing head before rebuilding an inside frame
trap: Leave the knees outside and recover the old foot grip first

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): What should you do when the partner lifts you off the mat?
flashcards.answer: Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.
flashcards.answer_line: Open the whole loop and disengage

plausible: Open the clasp but keep your elbow hooked to the leg
Release the hip frame while retaining the choking loop
trap: Wait for the lifted position to stabilize before letting go

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): Why turn onto your side before trying to connect the arm and leg?
flashcards.answer: Shoulder and hip frames permit a partial turn onto the ribs. That body angle brings elbow and knee closer without dragging the foot across a fixed knee.
flashcards.answer_line: It shortens the reach between the elbow and same-side knee

plausible: It lengthens the reaching arm while the knee stays distant
It moves the linking knee away from the shoulder
trap: It lets you keep the elbow wide once the hand connects

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): Why must a half-guard version be checked separately?
flashcards.answer: Top side control belongs to the choke defender. A half-guard finish requires its own leg configuration and is not automatically identical to the side-control setup.
flashcards.answer_line: Its leg relationship differs from the side-control setup

plausible: The free-leg path remains available even when that leg is trapped
The leg entanglement replaces the need for elbow-to-knee contact
trap: The half-guard hook supplies the same enclosure as the raised leg

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): Which adjustment threatens your own knee?
flashcards.answer: Wrenching the foot against a fixed knee substitutes joint torque for correct shoulder-to-hip closure.
flashcards.answer_line: Pulling the foot hard while the knee stays fixed

plausible: Framing at the hip to make side angle
Bringing the shoulder closer to the hip
trap: Releasing the loop when the partner rises

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (bottom): What helps limit the top player's posture while you remain grounded?
flashcards.answer: A forearm or shin across the hips can limit rising, but release immediately if the partner lifts you.
flashcards.answer_line: A forearm or shin frame across their hips

plausible: A hand on their shoulder with their hips unframed
Your arm-leg clasp alone with no contact at their hips
trap: Your free knee beside their hip without crossing its path

defender.name: Finish Buggy Choke Defender
defender.description: Finish Buggy Choke (defender): Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg. Use balanced posture and safe inside frames before the loop closes.
defender.overview:
The bottom player is beneath side control with an arm connected to the same-side leg around the opponent's head and one arm. Top side control belongs to the choke defender. A half-guard finish requires its own leg configuration and is not automatically identical to the side-control setup.

Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg. Use balanced posture and safe inside frames before the loop closes. Treat the choke as live even though you hold top side control.

Free the head-and-arm enclosure before changing to north-south or chasing another pin. Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape. Stop before dizziness or loss of normal responsiveness; top position does not make a secured choke safe.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Prevent hand-leg connection: Use balanced posture and safe inside frames before the loop closes.
Protect the neck: Treat the choke as live even though you hold top side control.
Clear before circling: Free the head-and-arm enclosure before changing to north-south or chasing another pin.
Do not slam or wrench: Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape.
Tap early: Stop before dizziness or loss of normal responsiveness; top position does not make a secured choke safe.

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (top): What early reach signals the bottom player's attack?
flashcards.answer: Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm past your head toward their same-side leg

plausible: Hand cupping your head with their leg still low
Both hands on their thigh with your head outside
trap: Knee rising beside your shoulder while the arm stays low

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (top): How can you deny the connection before it closes?
flashcards.answer: Use balanced posture and safe inside frames before the loop closes.
flashcards.answer_line: Maintain base and insert a frame inside the reaching path

plausible: Keep both arms outside their reaching elbow
Reach for the far shoulder before framing the raised leg
trap: Let the clasp close before trying to insert the frame

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (top): Why must you respect the choke from top side control?
flashcards.answer: Treat the choke as live even though you hold top side control.
flashcards.answer_line: Your head and arm can still be enclosed from below

plausible: Your shoulder pin forces the raised knee away from the elbow
Your chest pressure opens their supporting arm connection first
trap: Being beyond the knees keeps your neck outside the leg loop

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (top): What comes before circling to another pin?
flashcards.answer: Free the head-and-arm enclosure before changing to north-south or chasing another pin.
flashcards.answer_line: Release of the enclosure around your head and arm

plausible: A deeper crossface while the loop stays closed
One foot stepping past their head
trap: An open hand clasp with the elbow still hooked to the leg

flashcards.question: Finish Buggy Choke (top): Which response avoids turning defense into a fall or knee injury?
flashcards.answer: Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape.
flashcards.answer_line: Keep a grounded base and signal release if secured

plausible: Stand with the loop attached to stretch their reaching arm
Peel the linked foot while holding its knee in place
trap: Circle your base while leaving your head fixed inside
